scenes.name: up-poster-scroll-settle
scenes.note: Generated from tests/manifest.json::poster-scroll-settle. Finite fast scroll from the grid head to its deepest row (row 18 at most), followed by a complete art window. The scene sizes the sweep to the Library grid it boots into and logs the plan (`poster-gate: ... phase=planned`); the settled row must lie beyond the head's screenful, so it needs a grid of rows_per_screen+1 rows (4 rows = 19+ items at six columns, 1080p) with reachable artwork, and a smaller one fails as UNFIT CATALOG rather than as a regression. Motion FPS and zero new admissions for fast-moving cards are graded separately from the settled request/upload/render proof. No activation or viewing-history writes. The scene arms `plxnative-cardspeed=120`: the shipping app no longer declines a moving card, and this scene grades exactly that decline, so it turns the old gate back on. It also pins `plxnative-lookahead=0`: the shipping app warms the next rows at rest, and this scene's premise (the poster_gate.rs plan) is that the settled window was never warmed, so it turns the at-rest lookahead off. Oscillator-driven; no explicit key walk upstream.

scenes.name: up-poster-eviction-reversal

The source retains 64 slots; this scene exercises real byte-LRU eviction before source identity recycling, and the grade requires real evictions, evicted refusals in the reversal and rearms at rest. Needs 2x rows_per_screen grid rows (6 rows = 31+ items at six columns, 1080p); a smaller grid fails as UNFIT CATALOG. No activation or viewing-history writes. scenes.name: up-poster-hero-grid-dive
scenes.note: Generated from tests/manifest.json::poster-hero-grid-dive. Warm Home shelf 0 at its deepest card (column 11 at most), return to the hero, then dive back down the page's vertical travel. The shelf keeps its horizontal offset through all of it (a shelf draws at the offset it holds; the dive does not scale it), so the motion the dive hands the cards is the vertical alone. Shelf 0 is the only one the hero's DOWN door lands on, so the column, not the shelf, is sized to the catalog. The explicit 12 MiB texture ceiling makes the hero's art evict card art, so the dive must refuse the evicted art that comes back on screen while the page travels (`refused_*` in the dive phase, `moving_frames` >= 10, no admission while moving) and refill it at rest. Needs Home shelf 0 to hold the graded 1000 px offset, i.e. >=10 cards: the grader holds the shelf spring still through hero, dive and settle, which a shelf with no offset could not show; a shorter shelf fails as UNFIT CATALOG. Seeding focus onto a card activates nothing: no OK, no play, no viewing-history writes. The scene arms `plxnative-cardspeed=120`: the shipping app no longer declines a moving card, and this scene grades exactly that decline, so it turns the old gate back on. It also pins `plxnative-lookahead=0`: the shipping app warms the next rows at rest, and this scene's premise (the poster_gate.rs plan) is that the settled window was never warmed, so it turns the at-rest lookahead off. scenes.name: up-home-grid-deep
scenes.note: Generated from tests/manifest.json::home-grid-deep. Home with a hundred and seventy rows (#395), against the SYNTHETIC mock only: `./tests/run.py --fps --mock --filter home-grid-deep` starts tests/mock_pms.py --home-hubs 170 itself and needs no Plex account. plxnative-homeosc sweeps only ~9 rows either side of the top, so this scene instead presses Down once per LANDED row (the count is read from the `hubs: landed` log line, never hard-coded: a build with a card bound lands fewer rows than one without) at ~3 keys/s, rests, and presses Up back, and grades the heartbeats of THAT window. scenes.name: up-library-shelves-deep
scenes.note: Generated from tests/manifest.json::library-shelves-deep. The Library's Recommended page (`plxnative-libtype: recommended` presses the header's Recommended control; the Library page itself mounts no shelves) with a hundred and seventy recommended shelves, forty of them promoted collections (#412), against the SYNTHETIC mock only: `./tests/run.py --fps --mock --filter library-shelves-deep` starts tests/mock_pms.py --section-hubs 170 --section-hubs-linked 40 itself. This is the INSTRUMENT for #412: the section's shelf count has no cap, so all 170 land, and the scene FAILS if fewer than `walk.min_landed` (150) do (a build that bounds the Library at twelve shelves lands 12, and its shorter walk would otherwise pass on those 12). The walk length derives from what LANDED, as home-grid-deep's does: the shelf count is the seated section's `libhubs: section N landed M shelves` line (`plxnative-library` with no value seats the preferred Movies library, index 0), then one Down per shelf, a second for each linked shelf (its heading is a stop of its own, then its row) and `extra_rows` more (0: the page seats its first shelf on arrival and has no toolbar to cross; the Recommended page prints the Library's `focus route=library ... region=` fingerprint, `region=shelf row=R col=C` on a card, `heading`/`crumb`/`strip` elsewhere), at ~3 keys/s, a rest, and Up back; keys are only ever down/up. Graded: synthetic identity, keys sent == the expected count, a `focus route=library ... region=shelf` fingerprint (`plxnative-focus`, armed here) inside the walk window, a `region=shelf row=R` fingerprint there with R >= min_landed - 1 (the SCREEN must show a deep shelf, not only the store having landed 170, or a screen that capped its rows again would pass), loop_floor 50 and fps_floor 30 (library-scroll's) on that window. frame_gt33, the worst frame and p99 are printed, NOT graded (plxnative-framedrop is armed so the heartbeat carries them). max_rows >= 170 + 40 + extra_rows; run_secs covers it plus the launch wait (tests hold it to that). Run on the television (2026-10-20, ARM release build, panel on and muted, its own mock): PASS, 60 fps median over 8408 walk frames and 420 keys; the store's every-frame step (dstep) median 0.6 ms, p99 1.3 ms; no key press landed a late frame (frames of 25 ms or more are 0.30% of the window: the clear-stall waits, and the one landing frame of the 170th shelf). Key walk approximated from upstream's `walk` block; reach and landing assertions are not yet graded in the fork.

An INSTRUMENT, not a regression gate: how many LOADING (placeholder) poster tiles a viewer sees scrolling the Library grid in short bursts with rests between them, against the SYNTHETIC mock only (`./tests/run.py --fps --mock --filter library-burst`, a 1000-movie library). library-scroll's oscillator reverses every 350 ms and never rests, so it cannot show what a strategy that warms upcoming rows while the grid is AT REST buys; this does. The walk (tests/mock_fps.py `burst_plan`, the same KeyWalk machinery as the deep scenes, one ssh paced from the Mac, keys only down/up): `extra_rows` (2) Downs from the page header into the grid (the Library page mounts no shelves and logs no `libhubs` landing, so `walk.reach` lands the walk on its first `focus route=library` fingerprint), a rest, then 8 bursts of 4 Downs 125 ms apart each followed by 1.5 s of rest, then the same 8 bursts of Up back. The placeholder count is the `phcount: frames=F ph_frames=P draws=D ph=N` line the app writes once a second when `plxnative-phcount` is armed (rust-modules/src/dev/scenarios/phcount.rs, from ui::card_motion_metrics, which counts at the card primitive whether a card resolved a texture): ph is the card draws that showed a skeleton, i.e. placeholder tile-frames. PRINTED: ph in total, in the prelude, in the bursts and per burst (a sample belongs to the burst of the last key before it, so a burst owns the rest after it; good to about one line either side of a boundary), the share of card frames that showed one, median fps (and min/max), the usual frame_gt33/worst/p99 drops (plxnative-framedrop is armed so the heartbeat carries them) and the pupf/pupf_ge22/pup poster-upload tally; the generic loop= median is printed too. GRADED: only the synthetic identity line, keys sent == the expected count, and a `focus route=library ... region=grid` fingerprint (`plxnative-focus`) inside the walk window (plus the generic guard of at least 5 post-warmup loop samples). No floor, no ceiling: a candidate is compared by running the scene on both builds. Measured on the television (1000-movie mock, two runs each, placeholder tile-frames): 28,969 / 28,080 with no lookahead and the old moving-card decline (`lookahead=0 cardspeed=120`), 6,668 / 6,605 with 3 rows of lookahead, 3,552 / 2,948 with the decline off alone, 1,349 / 1,285 with both, which is the shipping default. Dev triggers pass through. The shipping defaults are 3 rows of at-rest poster lookahead and NO moving-card decline; `--extra-trigger plxnative-lookahead=0` measures the baseline without the lookahead (`=1`..`=4` another depth) and `--extra-trigger plxnative-cardspeed=120` brings the old moving-card decline back (it also takes any other px/s limit). `mock.movies` is 1000 (mock_pms.py's maximum) where library-scroll takes the default 48, so 32 grid rows of the walk exist. run_secs covers the walk's worst case plus the 10 s launch wait (tests hold it to that). Key walk approximated from upstream's `walk` block; reach and landing assertions are not yet graded in the fork.

scenes.name: up-home-idle
scenes.note: Generated from tests/manifest.json::home-idle. The inverse of every other fps scene: it asserts the app STOPS presenting. A settled Home grid must fall to at most fps_ceiling swaps/sec (ui::idle's KEEPALIVE_MS backstop is 2s, i.e. 0.5/s, so 3 leaves room for a late poster landing without letting a regression through). `loop_floor` still applies to loop=, which counts LOOP iterations, not presents: the loop must stay alive and responsive at >=30Hz while presenting nothing. A regression that re-armed the 60Hz repaint would blow the ceiling; one that wedged the loop would blow the loop_floor. warmup_s is 16, longer than the others, because the grid keeps presenting until the last poster has landed and its reveal spring has settled, and because Home's "Hold OK for options" hint (`ui::hold_hint`) is a legitimate animation on a resting tile: it dwells 1.5 s after the page settles, fades in, stands 6 s and fades out, so its whole life ends about 9-11 s after the page settles and the warmup must clear it (the hint has already retired itself by then; its fade beats above 3 fps would otherwise blow the ceiling). Do NOT pin the clock (`stillclock`) here: that would mask a perpetual-animator regression, which is what this scene exists to catch. Oscillator-driven; no explicit key walk upstream.

scenes.name: up-home-hint
scenes.note: Generated from tests/manifest.json::home-hint. The Home "Hold OK for options" hint (`ui::hold_hint`, a live-glass capsule) INSTRUMENT, against the SYNTHETIC mock only: `./tests/run.py --fps --mock --filter home-hint --save-logs <dir>` starts tests/mock_pms.py itself and needs no Plex account; no key is ever sent. plxnative-grid seats the first shelf tile and leaves it, so the hint's own schedule runs: focus rests (dwell 1.5 s), the capsule fades in (~0.4 s), stands (LIFE 6 s) and fades out on its own, which the 14 s window covers with the launch and the poster landings. A settled hint presents NO frames (idle gate), so a plain fps floor over a standing hint is blind to it; the frame cost is in the FADES and in anything that moves while it stands, which is why plxnative-framedrop is armed (25 ms: the heartbeat carries frame_n/frame_gt33/frame_max/frame_p99 only then) and the per-second numbers are read out of the saved log, NOT graded. Only liveness is graded (loop_floor 50). The screenshot pin (`stillclock`, `motion::phase_clocks_held`) must NOT be armed here: it pins the hint off (`HomeScreen::hint_input`). The hold fill (OK held ~0.5 s) is not exercised: the scene never sends ok. NOT yet graded on frame time; measure first. Oscillator-driven; no explicit key walk upstream.

scenes.name: up-modal-ramp
scenes.note: Generated from tests/manifest.json::modal-ramp. Settings opened and dismissed every 1.5 s through the real open/on_back (plxnative-modalosc), so the samples are the appear/disappear RAMP — host snapshot, scrim, ground — rather than a settled modal. No fps_floor: the ramp is ~200 ms of a 1500 ms period, so the median is legitimately low; the frame-TIME gate is the point. BASELINE 2026-09-06 panel-ON (TV session 1): worst robust_max=66.8 ms, max=67.4 — a Settings ramp frame costs ~67 ms today; the ceiling HOLDS that cost (fps floors are held, not raised, during the migration) and phase 11 is what brings it down. BIMODAL (TV session 2, 2026-09-06, phase 1b-ii): the same scene reads EITHER ~65 ms OR ~94 ms, on main's build AND the branch's, in one session (main: 96/94/67; branch: 93/93/65/84/96; a rebuild is byte-identical, so it is not the binary). In the slow mode the Settings-open frame charges ~52 ms to tick_drain (the update phase, where the host snapshot is taken) and ~41 ms to draw; in the fast mode ~10 ms and ~74 ms — the same work, differently placed, plus ~25 ms. Which mode a run lands in is not understood; the ceiling stays at the fast mode so the slow one is VISIBLE, and a single FAIL here is not evidence about a change until it is A/B'd against main in the same session. Oscillator-driven; no explicit key walk upstream.

scenes.name: up-deep-100
scenes.note: Generated from tests/manifest.json::deep-100. 100 pages pushed with NO pop in between (rotating Detail/Person through the real nav_push, opportunistically refreshing Person from the live cast row exactly as push-100 does, falling back to re-pushing Detail — never Library — until cast data lands), then 100 pops back to the root one page at a time — 200 `bench:` lines total, each ONE nav op (`dir=push|pop`) rather than push-100's open+close round trip. Library is NOT in the rotation: its only entry point (app::bridge::nav_tab -> NavOp::SelectTab) retires every entry above the root and mints at most one new one over it, so rotating it in would collapse the very depth this scene exists to build rather than deepen it — see dev::scenarios::bench::DeepBench's module doc. Found while building this scene: NavStack (ui/containers/stack.rs) bounds only the MOUNTED body count at CAP=16 (the oldest body below the top is evicted — Screen torn down, Unmount delivered — once more than 15 stay live below a new top), never the logical stack depth itself, which is unbounded; every Entry (id, arg, ReturnState) is retained regardless, so depth=100 pushes 100 real entries but only ever mounts <=16 of them at once, and a Pop past CAP remounts from the retained ReturnState. bench_depth_rss_kb grades exactly that: the deepest point minus the unwound root is the retained per-level state, which must stay small once eviction is doing its job. plxnative-framedrop is required for the same reason as push-100/modal-100. Oscillator-driven; no explicit key walk upstream.
